title: Doenjang Jjigae
summary: Doenjang stirred into an anchovy and kelp broth, with vegetables added. Doenjang is never boiled hard.
intro:
Doenjang jjigae is decided by the broth. Stir doenjang into plain water and all that is left is salt and soybean; use a broth made from dried anchovies and kelp and the same doenjang finishes long.

Ten minutes is all the broth needs, so do not skip this step.

items.name: Dried kelp (dasima / kombu)
items.amount: one 5 x 5 cm (2 x 2 in) piece

steps: Pull the heads and guts off the anchovies. Left in, the guts turn the broth bitter and muddy.
Put the water, anchovies and kelp in a pot and bring to the boil over medium heat. Once it boils, take out the kelp first. Kelp left in too long goes slimy.
Boil the anchovies for 5 minutes more, then lift them out. The broth is done.
Cut the potato into bite-sized pieces, the courgette into 1 cm (3/8 in) half-moons, the onion into thick pieces and the shiitake into thick slices.
Dissolve the doenjang into the broth through a sieve. If you have no sieve, put the paste in a ladle and loosen it with a little broth at a time.
Add the potato first and simmer over medium heat for 7 minutes. Potato takes the longest to cook.
Add the courgette, onion and shiitake and simmer for 5 minutes more.
Cut the tofu into 2 cm (3/4 in) cubes and add it, along with the minced garlic and chilli flakes. Simmer for 3 minutes.
Lay the diagonally sliced leek and chilli on top and turn off the heat after 1 minute. Taste, and if it is flat, add more doenjang 1/2 Tbsp (7.5 mL) at a time.
tips: Once the doenjang is in, do not boil it hard for long. The aroma goes and only a sour edge is left.
Home-made doenjang is saltier than the shop-bought kind, so start with 1 1/2 Tbsp (22 mL).
If you want meat in it, fry 50 g (about 2 oz) of beef brisket in sesame oil, then pour the broth over. Pork does not sit well with doenjang.
